readMeFirst: This is the FrameLink SD card register. There are three physical microSD cards and none of them is marked, so this file is the only way to answer 'which card is where and what is on it' without a human squinting at a card. It is written by `python tools/harness/fl.py cards` and is pointed at from progress.json's orientation block.

Run `python tools/harness/fl.py cards check` first. It reads whatever card is in the workstation's USB reader and compares it against what this file claims is in there. Exit 0 means the register and reality agree. Exit 2 means they do not, and the register is then not to be trusted until someone works out which of the two is wrong.

The operator has committed to not moving a card unless asked to. That commitment is what keeps this file true; `cards check` is what catches it if the commitment ever slips. After any card is moved, record it: `fl.py cards record --card <id> --kind <kind> --where '<text>' --why '<reason>'`. A move that is not recorded is a register that lies.

identityFields explains what each fingerprint field distinguishes and how to read it on Windows and on Linux. Read it before trusting a match: most of these fields identify the IMAGE on a card, not the card itself, so two cards flashed from the same file are indistinguishable by everything except the marker file. `cards check` reports 'ambiguous' rather than guessing when that happens.

The v1 card is irreplaceable. It is the only surviving v1 system, and reference/v1-state-inventory.txt is a capture taken from the machine it ran - captures cannot be re-taken once their source is gone. Never flash it, never format it, never let a flashing tool resolve to it.

reader.note: The reader is named by its USBSTOR device identity and never by drive letter or disk number - both are assigned at enumeration time and move. This is the same identity framelink-scratch/m25-image/flash-card.ps1 gates on. It contains the machine name, so on a different workstation this block must be re-established from `fl.py cards identify`, which lists every USB disk it can see.

cards.title: The original v1 frame's system card
cards.handling: Imaged, not yet redundant. Image 'v1-card-2026-08-23' is a full raw byte-for-byte capture of this card - 128,177,930,240 bytes, every sector including unallocated space, sha256 46703e3bdab19d8b7c3f4d0a5543cd5ae8d0fcb62666ef3203fef3e6beab0ecd, verified by a second full read of the card through a new handle, hashed independently, compared against a third independent hash of the written file. It exists in exactly one place (pc657: C:\Source\SixFive7\FrameLink\archive\v1-card-2026-08-23\framelink-v1-card.img), and one file on one disk is a copy rather than a backup - so until a second medium holds it, this card is still the only durable copy of the v1 system. Never flash it, never format it, never let a flashing tool resolve to it, and do not mount it writable. Record the second copy with `fl.py cards image --image v1-card-2026-08-23 --add-copy '<where>'`; this text is derived from that list and will change on its own when it does.

cards.fingerprintNote: Captured 2026-08-23 over SSH from the running frame, disturbing nothing. mbrSignature is the prefix of root=PARTUUID=c6a4cdf4-02 in /proc/cmdline. The sdCid/sdName/sdSerial fields come from /sys/block/mmcblk0/device/ and are the SD card's OWN factory identity - unique to the physical card, unlike every other field here, which belongs to the image or to whoever formatted it. They are readable only from a Pi: this project's USB reader does not pass the CID through, so `cards identify` in the reader can never see them. They are recorded because they are the only field that would still identify this card after a reflash changed everything else about it.

m25-2026-08-16.summary: The Fleet-Manager-generated FrameLink image for the M2.5 acceptance test - flash a card, boot it, watch a row appear in the adoption queue.
m25-2026-08-16.flashedBy: C:/Users/jori/framelink-scratch/m25-image/flash-card.ps1, from an elevated PowerShell. It names its target by bus type, model, exact capacity and USBSTOR identity - never by drive letter or disk number - and refuses on zero matches or on more than one.
m25-2026-08-16.source: framelink-scratch/m25-image/build-progress.log and base-image-prepare.log for the provenance; sizeBytes, sha256, mbrSignature and partitions were re-measured from the file itself on 2026-08-23 and agreed with the log.
m25-2026-08-16.warning: The generator writes files INTO the base image and does not repartition, so this image carries the BASE image's MBR signature. Every card written from any image built on the 2026-06-18 base therefore carries 041bba91, and after a flash mbrSignature can no longer tell two such cards apart. That is what the marker file in `fl.py cards label` is for.

v1-card-2026-08-23.summary: A full raw image of card 'v1' - The original v1 frame's system card. Every sector of the card, unallocated space included, uncompressed and in card order, so it restores by being written back byte for byte.
v1-card-2026-08-23.format: raw, uncompressed, whole device including the MBR and all unallocated space

verification.method: a second full read of the card through a new handle, hashed independently, compared against a third independent hash of the written file

v1-card-2026-08-23.restore: It is a whole-disk image including the MBR, so it is written back to a card with any raw writer - `dd if=<image> of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress` on Linux, or Raspberry Pi Imager's 'Use custom' on Windows - onto a card of at least 128,177,930,240 bytes. On Linux it also mounts without being restored: `losetup -Pfr --show <image>` attaches it read-only with its partitions.

gate.contents: The v1 frame's complete system as it ran before this project began. This is the origin of the parity target: reference/v1-state-inventory.txt was captured from the machine that booted this card.

mbrSignature.what: The four-byte MBR disk signature at offset 0x1B8, lower-case hex. This is the prefix of every PARTUUID on the card, so `root=PARTUUID=f870549c-02` in a cmdline.txt names signature f870549c.
mbrSignature.linux: lsblk -no PTUUID /dev/sdX   # or blkid -s PTUUID -o value /dev/sdX

capacityBytes.what: Total capacity as the storage stack reports it. Use Get-Disk, not Win32_DiskDrive: the latter reports TotalSectors*512 rounded down to whole cylinders and came back 3,392,000 bytes smaller on the card measured here, which is enough to make a naive equality check fail against itself.

partitions.what: One entry per primary partition: MBR type byte, byte offset and byte length. A Raspberry Pi OS card is 0x0c (FAT32 LBA) then 0x83 (Linux); a factory card is one 0x07 exFAT partition.
partitions.windows: Get-Partition -DiskNumber N | Select MbrType, Offset, Size

volumeSerials.what: The filesystem volume serial of each mountable partition - exFAT/FAT store a 32-bit serial in the boot record, ext4 a UUID. Set by whoever formatted the filesystem, which for a never-flashed card is the factory.
volumeSerials.linux: blkid -s UUID -o value /dev/sdXn   # FAT serials print as 2C32-CEEB

volumeLabels.what: The filesystem label of each mountable partition. Empty on the factory card; 'bootfs' and 'rootfs' on a Raspberry Pi OS card.

marker.what: The contents of FRAMELINK-CARD.txt in the card's FAT boot partition, if this harness has written one. The only field that is unique to a card by construction, because the value is chosen rather than observed.
marker.linux: cat /boot/firmware/FRAMELINK-CARD.txt   # or from the mounted boot partition

sdCid.what: The SD CID register - manufacturer, OEM, product name, revision, serial and production date, burned in at manufacture and genuinely unique per card. NOT AVAILABLE through the USB reader on this workstation: the Realtek bridge reports an empty SerialNumber and passes no CID through. Readable only from a Pi, whose native SD controller exposes it. Recorded here so that a session on a frame knows it is worth capturing.
sdCid.windows: not available through a USB card reader
sdCid.linux: cat /sys/block/mmcblk0/device/cid   # on the Pi itself, no root needed
